title: Stop allocating a new key for every span attribute

blocks.text: The service's tracing library records a span for every database call and every HTTP request, and each span asks `AttributeKey.of(...)` for the keys of its attributes. An allocation profile of the checkout service shows `AttributeKey` among the top three allocated classes: hundreds of thousands of keys a minute, nearly all of them for the four names in `STANDARD`.

Finish `of(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/AttributeKey.java`. When you're done, every call for a standard name returns the same key object, wherever the name string came from. Any other name still gets a key with that name, and nothing of it is kept afterwards, however many different names the application sends. Keep the shared keys in `KEYS`, which `kept()` reports. About two lines in total.

cases.says: every key carries the name it was asked for, and equal names give equal keys
a standard name gives the same key object on every call, even when the name is built at run time
ten thousand different non-standard names leave nothing more kept than the standard keys

origin.section: new Always Allocates; a Static Factory Can Hand Back an Object It Already Made

concepts: A static factory can hand back an object it already made where new must allocate; sharing is safe only for immutable objects, and a cache keyed by caller input must stay bounded.
